CLIENT ENGAGEMENT · NTT INDYCAR · 10 MONTHS

{`How an Information Architecture Rebuild and App Redesign Increased INDYCAR Fan Retention by 30% `}

INDYCAR wanted younger fans, and its app wasn’t helping. New fans couldn’t tell where to start, and regulars had to dig for race information. I led the UX work that rebuilt the app’s structure around a beginner’s guide, then turned rules, cars and drivers into things to explore instead of read.

ROLE

Lead UX Designer

TIMELINE

10 months

TEAM

2 UX researchers, 1 UI designer, me

TOOLS

Figma, Miro, Google Analytics, Maze

some detail held back under NDA

One place to dive into INDYCAR experience

02 · CONTEXT

A fast sport with an app that felt slow

F1, the NBA and WWE had already shown a generation what a sports app should feel like. INDYCAR’s app gave basic race information and little else, so Gen Z and millennial fans had no easy way in.

THE CHALLENGE

INDYCAR is fast, thrilling and high-stakes. But its digital experience? It wasn’t keeping up.

OUR MISSION

Reimagine the INDYCAR digital experience to engage the next generation of fans.

03 · PROBLEM AND GOALS

New fans got lost, and regulars couldn’t find race info

Three problems kept coming up. Each one became a goal.

THE PROBLEM

THE GOAL

01

New fans didn’t know where to start.

Grow a younger fan base without losing the fans INDYCAR already had.

02

Existing fans struggled to find key race information.

Cut bounce rates and keep people in the app for longer.

03

The app had none of the rush of a live race.

Make the app exciting enough that fans want to come back.

04 · DISCOVERY

Weak information architecture buried the basics under menus and text

Fans, new and old, wanted to learn more about the sport, from the rules to the cars, and couldn’t find where. The app already had a section for exactly that: INDYCAR 101. It sat in the hamburger menu, near Settings. The plan was to move it somewhere prominent, so we first audited the section itself to see what else was holding it back.

What is INDYCAR?

Car specs

Qualifying

Flags

a spec sheet, not a car

Ambiguous navigation

Inside the menu, INDYCAR 101 looked like any other link, with nothing to say it was the place to start.

Content overload

Car specs were dense blocks of text with almost nothing to look at.

Disorganised layout

Rules and regulations had no clear structure, so they took real effort to get through.

05 · RESEARCH

Fans weren’t disengaged. They were overwhelmed.

Too many taps and too much text stood between a new fan and the thrill of a race. Younger fans were already drawn to F1, and INDYCAR’s marketing didn’t travel as far, so the app had to win them over on its own.

WHAT OTHER LEAGUES GET RIGHT · F1, NBA, CRICKET, WWE

Stories, not specs

F1 and WWE put the athletes and the cars at the centre. That builds an emotional connection a spec table never will.

Short video and live stats

The NBA, cricket and WWE keep fans around with short clips and stats they can play with.

Exploring beats reading

Gen Z fans tune out static text. They stay when there’s something to tap, swipe or watch.

“We want fans to feel the speed, the intensity… but online, they just feel stuck.”

{`David Craske, Head of Digital Experiences & Strategies, INDYCAR`}

this became the brief

06 · INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE

One front door for new fans, six paths from there

I led a full rebuild of the sitemap. INDYCAR 101 got a clear home page with six sections under it: driving, how a race works, the car, tracks, teams and drivers.

INDYCAR 101 gets its own front door

Clear hierarchy

Visual, interactive content comes first in every section, with the detail one level down.

Streamlined navigation

Restructured sections so fans hold less in their heads while they find their way.

07 · PROCESS

Crazy 8s first, then wireframes the fan team could react to

We brainstormed with Crazy 8s, turned the strongest ideas into rough sketches and lo-fi wireframes, and validated them with INDYCAR stakeholders and the fan engagement team.

Sketches from the Crazy 8s round

Lo-fi wireframes: INDYCAR 101, a guide to tyres and the shorts view

08 · ITERATIONS

Round one put more on screen. Round two made it faster to use.

We ran two major design iterations, and usability tests shaped each one.

ITERATION 1

More on every screen

Raised information density so more fits at a glance.

Swapped text-heavy sections for images and video.

Added interactive elements that tailor what each fan sees.

ITERATION 2

Faster to use

Tuned the density for quicker interactions.

Embedded video and infographics in place of long text.

Added swipeable car breakdowns, interactive race strategy guides and behind-the-scenes content.

09 · FINAL DESIGNS

Rules, cars and drivers became things to explore

Five features carry the redesign. Each one swaps a block of text for something visual or interactive.

Beginner’s guide

Shows new fans what makes INDYCAR different, in a layout built to be scanned and tapped.

Anatomy of a race car

An interactive model of the car. Pick a part to see how it works.

Teams and behind the scenes

Exclusive footage of pit crews, engineers and race-day prep.

Driver profiles

Career timelines, exclusive footage and stats that give fans a driver to follow.

a car you can take apart

Rules and track guides

Visual breakdowns of flags, track types and race strategy, in place of the old wall of rules.

10 · OUTCOMES

In testing, sessions ran 30% longer and bounces fell 25%

We validated the designs through user testing, heuristic evaluation, cognitive walkthroughs and stakeholder feedback.

Engagement in testing

30%

increase in session duration

25%

drop in bounce rate

Usability

4.8/5

System Usability Score (SUS)

85%

of users preferred the new interactive features

Stakeholders

4.9/5

stakeholder rating of the approach

“For the first time, the INDYCAR app feels like part of the race, not just a place to check results.”

Fan feedback on the redesign

11 · REFLECTION

The hardest part was balance. INDYCAR’s executives had business goals, fans wanted to feel the race, and marketing and design each had their own priorities. I worked closely with all of them and let test results drive every iteration. It taught me to argue for UX in business discussions, and to design for engagement that lasts.

WHAT COMES NEXT

3D car model

a fully interactive version of the race car

More video

expanded video content

Behind the scenes

more footage of teams and race-day prep
